page: Amazon Web Services c8gd.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical ARM64 cores based on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, operating at 2.7 GHz. The instance is equipped with 384 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per core allocation. It includes 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, managed via the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

In multi-core benchmarks, the c8gd.48xlarge demonstrates top-tier performance. Multi-core stress-ng CPU tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the top 10% of benchmarked servers. Memory performance is also highly rated, with cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching 21,316.19 GB/sec and uncached large block write bandwidth at 402.56 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations show exceptional throughput, with Redis handling 362.69 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and LLM inference for small models are relatively average or weak, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to leverage this hardware effectively.

Given its ARM64 architecture and high physical core density, the c8gd.48xlarge offers high compute efficiency per watt and resource unit compared to traditional x86 architectures. The inclusion of 11.4 TB of local NVMe SSD storage eliminates the need for external block storage for high-I/O workloads, enhancing qualitative cost-efficiency. This instance is highly suited for large-scale parallel computing, high-throughput database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and memory-intensive data processing workloads that benefit from localized high-speed storage.
